assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clean discovery from nature: the baryon acoustic peak in galaxy clustering is a standard ruler that turns dark energy from an inference into a measured expansion history. It is original, conceptually simple and has been the backbone of precision cosmology for two decades. For someone who thinks the dark-energy question is central and that physics needs clues from data, this is the type of result that speaks for itself.
assessment.attribution: The 2005 detections came from SDSS (Eisenstein and collaborators) and 2dFGRS (Cole, Peacock and the 2dF team), so Eisenstein, Cole and Peacock are a defensible trio. Theoretical roots in the CMB acoustic physics (Peebles-Yu, Sunyaev-Zeldovich) lie outside the credited names and may complicate a purist view of credit.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: reproduced by BOSS, eBOSS, 6dFGS, WiggleZ and DESI, with consistent results across samples and methods. Recent DESI hints of evolving dark energy rest on BAO, which raises its importance rather than undermining it. Timely.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants the BAO measurement itself or the broader programme of survey cosmology.
Credit between the SDSS and 2dFGRS teams and the large collaborations is not fully clean.
Earlier cosmology prizes (2006, 2011, 2019) may make the committee wary of repetition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a vast field: the quantum spin Hall effect predicted by Kane and Mele, confirmed in HgTe, and extended to three dimensions. It is original, conceptually deep and has become a template for topological band theory with real experimental realisations.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposal; Molenkamp's group delivered the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction. Hasan's 3D observations and the BHZ/Zhang contribution, as well as Moore, Balents and Roy, make the allocation of credit contentious; the supplied names allow only a theory-plus-experiment trio.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with more than fifteen years of independent confirmation across many materials, though applications remain limited. Recognition is timely, although the 2016 prize already covered topological phases.
uncertainties: Disputed credit for the 3D case and for the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction, which sits outside the credited names.
Overlap with the 2016 topological phase-transition prize.
Whether the committee would split spin Hall from 3D topological insulators.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on the magic-wavelength idea, has pushed timekeeping to the 10^-18 level and enables tests of fundamental constants, relativistic redshift at millimetre scales and potential searches for dark matter. It is a concrete experimental discovery with clear importance.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and realised it; Ye's group drove it to record accuracy. The two-person configuration is clean, though Hall and Hansel have already been honoured for frequency combs and others contributed to trapping and clock-laser work.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and independently reproduced in many laboratories, with a redefinition of the second under discussion. Timely.
uncertainties: Whether this counts as a discovery or as a precision instrument development.
Overlap with the 2005 frequency comb and 2012 prizes.
Contributions from Pottier, Takamoto and others are not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's detection of a diffuse high-energy astrophysical neutrino flux, and the later identification of TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy and probes cosmic-ray origin. A real observational discovery from nature with existential significance for high-energy astrophysics.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube; Karle was central to the detector and analysis. The collaboration is large, and the supplied two names omit other leaders, but a two-person prize is conceivable. Possible alternative: recognition of the project through Halzen alone.
assessment.maturity: Strong: the diffuse flux has been confirmed repeatedly, and the Galactic-plane result is recent. Source identification remains incomplete, but the discovery itself is sound. Timing is reasonable, not overripe.
uncertainties: Individual attribution within a large collaboration.
Source population of most neutrinos is still unresolved.
Role of the earlier Baikal and AMANDA projects.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* directly show black-hole shadows and test strong-field gravity. The result is vivid and has existential resonance, though the physics findings so far largely confirm general relativity.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept, Doeleman led the array development and Moran built the VLBI foundations. Over 200 collaborators contributed, and Event Horizon Telescope credit is distributed; any three-person selection is partly arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: two sources, polarisation and multiyear M87 data are consistent, but the physical constraints remain modest and the scientific harvest is early.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit is not reducible to three people.
Scientific novelty beyond confirming general relativity is limited so far.
Prior recognition of black-hole physics in 2020.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background from pulsar timing arrays opens a new gravitational-wave band, probably from supermassive black hole binaries. A genuine discovery from nature with strong cosmological and astrophysical implications.
assessment.attribution: The credited names represent pulsar-timing leaders (Kramer for EPTA, McLaughlin for NANOGrav, Manchester for PPTA), but the decisive contributors include the founders of the timing technique and several collaboration leads; the allocation is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Premature in my view: the Hellings-Downs correlation sits at about 3 to 4 sigma in individual arrays and the origin, astrophysical or cosmological, is not settled. A few more years of combined data would strengthen the case considerably.
uncertainties: Statistical significance is below the usual discovery standard.
Origin of the signal unresolved.
Allocation among three regional collaborations is contentious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP's all-sky maps fixed the cosmological parameters to percent level, established the flat LCDM concordance and measured reionisation and the acoustic peaks. It set the standard for precision cosmology and is a clear data-driven landmark.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page led instrument design and Spergel led the cosmological interpretation. This is a natural trio, though others such as Wilkinson and Hinshaw also made major contributions.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and confirmed by Planck and ground-based experiments. The delay may mean that COBE and other cosmology prizes have absorbed much of the recognition.
uncertainties: The 2006 COBE prize and 2019 cosmology prize may reduce appetite for another CMB award.
Credit within a large collaboration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene shows correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable flat band, creating the field of twistronics. It is original, with a theoretical prediction followed by striking experiments.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group observed correlated insulators and superconductivity in 2018. Cao and Fatemi, who did the experiments, and others are not in the credited names. The pairing of prediction and experiment is straightforward.
assessment.maturity: Only eight years old, with broad independent replication but incomplete understanding of the superconducting mechanism. Likely a bit early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism is still debated.
Sample-to-sample variability.
Recognition may be premature relative to the other candidates.
